### How Layers Work in Tile Maps

plotly.js no longer uses Mapbox: the `scattermapbox`, `choroplethmapbox` and
`densitymapbox` traces and `layout.mapbox` were replaced by the MapLibre-based
`scattermap`, `choroplethmap` and `densitymap` traces (`add_scattermap()`,
`add_choroplethmap()`, `add_densitymap()`) and `layout.map` (`go_map()`).
If your figure contains one or more of these traces, the `layout` of your
figure contains configuration information for the map itself.

The map is composed of layers of three different types.

1. `layout.map.style` defines the lowest layers, also known as your "base map"
2. the traces added with `add_scattermap()` and friends are by default rendered above the base map (this can be controlled via the use of `below` attribute).
3. the `layout.map.layers` attribute accepts an array of `go_map_layer()` objects that are by default rendered above the traces (this can be controlled via the `below` attribute).

### Access Tokens

MapLibre does not need a Mapbox Access Token. All of the built-in values of
`layout.map.style` work without one:

1. `white-bg` yields an empty white canvas which results in no external HTTP requests
2. `open-street-map`, `carto-positron`, `carto-darkmatter`, `carto-voyager` (and their `-nolabels` variants), `basic`, `streets`, `outdoors`, `light`, `dark`, `satellite` and `satellite-streets` yield maps composed of tiles from various public tile servers which do not require signups or access tokens

`layout.map.style` can also be a style URL or a style object as defined in the [MapLibre style spec](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-style-spec/).

#### Using `layout.map.layers` to Specify a Base Map

If you have access to your own private tile servers, or wish to use a tile server not included in the list above, the recommended approach is to first set `layout.map.style` to `"white-bg"` and then set `layout.map.layers` to `below` to specify a custom base map.

> If you omit setting `layout.map.layers` to `below`, when using this approach, your data will likely be hidden by fully-opaque raster tiles!

### OpenStreetMap Tiles

This chart demonstrates how to use "open-street-map" tiles as the base map for a chart.

> The "open-street-map" style loads tiles from OpenStreetMap's volunteer-run
> servers, whose [tile usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/)
> blocks requests that don't identify the page they come from. Browsers or
> extensions that strip the `Referer` header then show an "Access blocked"
> tile instead of the map. The `carto-*` styles have no such requirement, so
> the other examples on these pages use `"carto-voyager"`.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

us_cities <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/us-cities-top-1k.csv")

us_cities |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scattermap(
    lat = ~lat,
    lon = ~lon,
    marker = go_scattermap_marker(color = "fuchsia"),
    hovertext = ~City
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      style = "open-street-map",
      zoom = 2.5,
      center = go_map_center(lon = -88, lat = 34)
    )
  )
```

### Base Map Below A Trace

This chart demonstrates how to use a public USGS imagery map as a base map using `layout.map.layers`. The map is rendered *below* the trace.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

us_cities <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/us-cities-top-1k.csv")

us_cities |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scattermap(
    lat = ~lat,
    lon = ~lon,
    hovertext = ~City,
    marker = go_scattermap_marker(color = "fuchsia")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      style = "white-bg",
      zoom = 3,
      center = go_map_center(lon = -93, lat = 41),
      layers = list(
        go_map_layer(
          below = "traces",
          sourcetype = "raster",
          source = list("https://basemap.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/USGSImageryOnly/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}")
        )
      )
    )
  )
```

#### Maps Below and Above A Trace

This example uses the same base map *below* the trace as the one above. 

In addition, a WMS layer map from Environment Canada (which displays near-real-time radar imagery in partly-transparent raster tiles) is rendered *above* the `scattermap` trace, as is the default:

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

us_cities |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scattermap(
    lat = ~lat,
    lon = ~lon,
    hovertext = ~City,
    marker = go_scattermap_marker(color = "fuchsia")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      style = "white-bg",
      zoom = 3,
      center = go_map_center(lon = -93, lat = 41),
      layers = list(
        go_map_layer(
          below = "traces",
          sourcetype = "raster",
          source = list("https://basemap.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/USGSImageryOnly/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}")
        ),
        go_map_layer(
          sourcetype = "raster",
          source = list("https://geo.weather.gc.ca/geomet/?SERVICE=WMS&VERSION=1.3.0&REQUEST=GetMap&BBOX={bbox-epsg-3857}&CRS=EPSG:3857&WIDTH=1000&HEIGHT=1000&LAYERS=RADAR_1KM_RDBR&TILED=true&FORMAT=image/png")
        )
      )
    )
  )
```

#### Dark Base Map

This example uses the "carto-darkmatter" base map. Unlike the old Mapbox
"dark" style, it doesn't need an access token.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

us_cities <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/us-cities-top-1k.csv")

us_cities |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scattermap(
    lat = ~lat,
    lon = ~lon,
    marker = go_scattermap_marker(color = "fuchsia"),
    hovertext = ~City
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      style = "carto-darkmatter",
      zoom = 2.5,
      center = go_map_center(lon = -88, lat = 34)
    )
  )
```

#Reference

See `go_scattermap()` and `go_map()` for more information and options!
